interpretation: The oracle returns 3.61 on average and goes to the trapped region (11.27 m) from 4095 of 4096 starts (stops at once: 1, of which 1 start inside it), in 2.8 moves (at most 5): the 0.2 deg trapped spot is a few ladder steps from anywhere in the box, so the 31 / 57 / 89 patterns are never worth stopping at for a fully informed agent. The image-only scripted policy returns 0.78 (22 % of the oracle, regret 2.83): it always ends at >= 31 bounces and at >= 57 in 55.0 %, but trapped in only 2.9 %, and spends 32 steps (0.31 of return in step costs); brightness is nearly constant within the 31 plateau (141-146) and the 57 island (216-219), so the 0.2 deg 89 / trapped spots are found only when a probe happens to land in them. For this heuristic the blind region is cheap: the 1 deg spiral reaches >= 31 bounces after 3.2 steps on average from blind starts, and the regret is 2.90 (blind) vs 2.78 (informative); the oracle needs 3.37 vs 2.46 moves (returns are higher from blind starts only because P_0 is lower). The image-free homing policy returns 3.58 (99 % of the oracle): with one fixed geometry the mount limit gives the absolute tilt (the clamp shows in obs['action'], and 4 pushes force it anyway), so stage 1 is solvable open-loop from a memorized map; PPO can learn exactly that, so stage-1 success alone does not show that the policy reads the images. Random policies have negative returns (-0.57 with stop, -0.72 without): step costs and wandering off the plateau outweigh the rare visits to long paths.
